Query Fabric SQL as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__fabric.R
oauth_db_fabric_sql.Rd

Read data from a Fabric Warehouse, Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint, or SQL Database with DBI. The default ODBC backend also supports dbplyr. Queries use the visitor's Microsoft account.

Usage

oauth_db_fabric_sql(
  authorization,
  server,
  database = NULL,
  ...,
  backend = c("odbc", "adbc"),
  target = "sql",
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

server

Database hostname.

database

Database name.

...

Arguments for fabricQueryR::fabric_sql_connect(), such as read_only and timeout.

backend

SQL driver interface: "odbc" (default) or "adbc".

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning a DBI connection.

Details

Install fabricQueryR and the SQL driver. Copy the server and database from the item's SQL connection settings. Use oauth_db_microsoft_client() with services = "sql" for sign-in.

Create con inside server() and get connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression before querying. The helper reuses the connection and closes it when the authorization or session ends.

SQL drivers

The default ODBC backend supports DBI and dbplyr. To use ADBC for DBI or Arrow queries, install adbi, adbcdrivermanager and the external MSSQL driver (version 1.5.0 or later), then pass backend = "adbc". Use ODBC for dbplyr's SQL Server translations; the ADBC connection does not currently select that dialect.

ADBC connections reopen with a current token when con() is next called after token renewal. This closes outstanding results on the old connection. Consume and release results before starting another operation.

Direct DBI reads use the driver's type conversions. For fabricQueryR's exact numeric conversion, call fabricQueryR::fabric_sql_query() through oauth_db_fabric_api() with backend = "adbc" and numeric_policy = "exact".

See also

oauth_db_microsoft_client(), oauth_db_fabric_api(). vignette("fabric", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_oracle(), oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_redshift(), oauth_db_snowflake(), oauth_db_sql_server(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_fabric_sql(
  auth$connection,
  server = "example.datawarehouse.fabric.microsoft.com",
  database = "Reporting"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT TOP (20) name FROM sys.tables")
})
} # }
